transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lyndi Kenyon.
House Republicans have elected Ohio's Jim Jordan as the next minority leader.
The Ohio Republican was elected via secret ballot behind closed doors
and takes on the role when the next Congress convenes in January.
Inflation in October was hotter than forecasters anticipated,
NPR's Scott Horsley reports.
Consumer prices in October were up four-tenths of a percent from September.
That's a smaller increase than the previous month,
but inflation's still higher than forecasters had expected.
Food prices increased sharply during the month, as did the cost of housing.
Stripping out volatile food and energy prices,
core inflation was three-tenths of a percent, also higher than forecasters had predicted.
The hot inflation reading underscores investors' expectation
that the Federal Reserve will raise its benchmark interest rate next month.
Markets were expecting a quarter-point increase,
but Fed Governor Chris Waller suggested today
an even bigger rate hike might be appropriate to help bring prices under control.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
Lawmakers elected last month in Israel were sworn in today.
Opponents of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
now hold the majority of the seats in Israel's parliament, the Knesset.
NPR's Lauren Freya reports.
A military band played as Israeli lawmakers filed in and took their oaths of office.
Most have pledged to support Prime Minister Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eizenkot.
Israel's President Isaac Herzog encouraged rival parties
to extend a hand of compromise and build a governing coalition.
Eizenkot is under pressure to break a campaign promise
with Arab-led parties, whom Netanyahu lashed out at again,
accusing them without evidence of fraud and of endangering Israel.
Some Arab lawmakers walked out when Israel's national anthem played.
Lawmakers have submitted bills to impose term limits
and repeal Netanyahu's judicial reforms.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
A scientific body of the Pan-American Health Organization is meeting this week
to determine whether measles has once again become endemic in the U.S.
NPR's Maria Godoy reports.
The panel will decide whether the U.S. should lose its official designation
as a country that has eliminated measles.
The deliberations come as vaccination rates are down in the U.S.
with nearly 5,200 measles cases reported this year.
Eight measles-related deaths have been reported in three states.
Dr. Amos Hidalja with the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security says
losing the designation raises bigger questions
about the country's ability to master infectious disease problems.
If you can't control something like measles,
which has had a medical countermeasure available since the 1960s,
what does that mean for any kind of new or emerging pathogen that might arise?
You're listening to NPR News.
The last independent newspaper working in Russia closed its doors yesterday.
NPR's Charles Maines reports the newspaper was a final holdout
against state pressure on media.
For more than 30 years, Novi Gazeta defended democratic ideals in Russia
and criticized authorities when they fell short of them, sometimes at great cost.
Six Novi Gazeta journalists, including star investigative reporter Anna Politkoskaya,
were killed on the job.
But there were moments of triumph, too.
Novi Gazeta's then editor-in-chief, Dmitry Murata,
was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021 for the paper's defense of press freedoms.
Novi continued working in Russia despite censorship laws
introduced amid the war in Ukraine.
Yet in announcing the paper's closure,
staff said the Kremlin had finally suffocated the paper's finances
and ability to report without going to prison.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
A member of the U.S. Army has been arrested by British counterterrorism police
on charges of espionage related to Russia.
The Metropolitan Police say the 41-year-old man was arrested near Gloucester.
Counterterrorism police in the U.K. are working closely with the U.S. military
and with the FBI.
Meanwhile, FBI Director Kash Patel released a statement saying, quote,
"This important arrest involves allegations of espionage,
which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies."
Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans described the arrest
in her words as "significant."
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: House Republicans elect Ohio's Jim Jordan as next minority leader in secret ballot
October consumer prices rise 0.4% from September, hotter than forecasters expected
Fed Governor Chris Waller suggests larger interest rate hike may be appropriate
Israeli lawmakers sworn in, most opposing Prime Minister Netanyahu's government
Pan-American Health Organization panel weighs whether US has lost measles elimination status
Russia's last independent newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, closes after state pressure
British counterterrorism police arrest U.S. Army member on Russia-related espionage charges
